key_insight: VisGym provides a unified, configurable suite of 17 environments that reveal how Vision–Language Models perform across long-horizon, multi-step visual interactions by letting researchers control perception, memory, and action variables.
problem_solved: Current VLMs are poorly characterized in extended, interactive tasks; there is no scalable, customizable benchmark to evaluate and train models on integrated perception–memory–action behavior over long planning horizons.
method: Design and release a gym of 17 diverse environments (symbolic puzzles, real-image tasks, navigation, manipulation) covering varied modalities and interaction types.
Expose fine-grained controls for difficulty, input representations, planning horizon, and feedback to enable targeted evaluation and curriculum learning.
Provide multi-step solvers, training/evaluation protocols, and metrics to measure integrated perception, memory, and action performance across environments.
impact: VisGym enables reproducible, scalable benchmarking and targeted training for multimodal agents, helping researchers diagnose long-horizon failures and iterate on architectures and training strategies that integrate perception, memory, and action.

paper_title: VisGym: Diverse, Customizable, Scalable Environments for Multimodal Agents
paper_authors: Zirui Wang, Junyi Zhang, Jiaxin Ge, Long Lian, Letian Fu
